description: Maniac (loose-aggressive) plays far too many hands and bets and raises far too often. It starts from the trainer's own advice, like TAG, but often raises hands the advice folds, raises where the advice only calls, and bets most of the time when everyone checks to it. It still calls when the betting is capped, and after the flop it calls most bets the pot odds say to fold, so it pays off your value bets. Call it down with good hands and bet your strong ones for value.

deviations.justification: Raising nearly half of the hands the chart folds against a bet more than doubles TAG's starting range and makes most of those entries raises, which puts the Maniac's VPIP and PFR inside their bands.
Turning most of the chart's calls into raises means the Maniac rarely just calls before the flop, so its raises carry little information about its hand strength.
In the big blind with only limpers in, the Maniac usually raises its free option, punishing limps and building pots it cannot win on hand strength alone.

Betting more often than not when it is checked to, whatever it holds, is the Maniac's defining leak: its bets show little strength, so the learner should call down lighter, and the checks it keeps hold its postflop aggression inside its 65 to 85 percent band.

Raising some of the bets it would call keeps the pot growing with drawing and medium hands, while calling the rest keeps its postflop aggression inside its 65 to 85 percent band now that opponents so often fold or check to it.

Calling most bets the pot odds say to fold makes the Maniac pay off value bets with weak hands, which is how a real maniac gives back the chips it wins with steals and keeps its aggression from reaching every street.
